summary: Orbit Wellness is a responsive, single-file website that introduces people to the health challenges of living off Earth and offers practical, everyday ways to manage them. It covers four settings: a spacecraft in transit, a low-Earth-orbit space station, a surface base on another planet, and a Moon base. A short check-in survey moves from general questions about sleep, mood and energy to ones specific to the habitat, and ends with general, non-clinical suggestions and a clear reminder that it is not a diagnostic tool. A body guide follows, in which users select one of fourteen muscle areas on a front and back drawing and receive training or pain-relief exercises adapted to the gravity and equipment of that habitat. The design uses a navy background with NASA-inspired red and white accents, Roboto typography, custom habitat illustrations, a supplied logo, and restrained motion for page changes and text reveals that is switched off for people who prefer reduced motion. The content is stored as editable data separate from the layout, which makes the site straightforward to extend. The exercise text is general guidance that would benefit from review by a qualified professional before publication, and the site has not yet been tested in a browser.
details: We built Orbit Wellness because we kept wondering what it would actually feel like to stay healthy somewhere with no hospital nearby. The site lets you pick a place to live: a spacecraft, a space station, a base on another planet, or a base on the Moon. Each place has its own page that explains what tends to go wrong there. Bones and muscles weaken, sleep gets disrupted, radiation exposure builds up, and being stuck with the same few people for months wears on your mood. Next to that are simple daily habits that help. There is also a short survey that starts with general questions about sleep, mood and energy and then asks a couple about the habitat you chose. It gives you a few gentle suggestions at the end, and it says clearly that it is not a diagnosis. Below the survey is a body guide, where you tap a muscle group on a front and back figure and get exercises to either build strength or ease discomfort, adjusted for where you are. A squat on the Moon, for example, is a different job from resistance work in free fall. We hope people come away knowing a bit more about how space changes the body, and with a few habits they might even use on Earth. It runs in any browser, and the text lives in simple lists, so an expert can change a tip or an exercise without touching the design. We wrote it in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, drew the illustrations and body figure as SVG, used the Roboto font and our own logo, and had Claude, an AI assistant from Anthropic, help us write the code. We chose navy, red and white because they feel like NASA, and we gave every habitat its own artwork instead of reusing one picture. While building it we kept coming back to safety, so the site lists warning signs like sharp pain, numbness or chest pain that mean you should get real medical help. We also made it work with a keyboard and for people who prefer less motion, and we checked that it fits on a phone screen. The exercise advice is general and has not been reviewed by a professional yet, so that is the next step before we share it widely.
